title: Quenched Uruguayan Beef Empanada
description: A flavorful and savory empanada filled with slow-cooked meat, onions, and herbs, served with a tangy briny bechamel sauce.
instructions: Heat the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the parsley, salt, and pepper.
In a separate saucepan, bring the beef stock to a simmer over medium heat.
In a small bowl, whisk together the flour and a splash of the hot stock to make a roux.
Add the roux to the saucepan and whisk until smooth.
Cook for 2 minutes, or until the sauce thickens.
Remove from heat and stir in the Gruy3re cheese until melted.
To assemble the empanadas, place a spoonful of the meat mixture onto one half of a dough circle, leaving a 1/2 inch border around the edges.
Moisten the edges with water and fold the dough over the filling, pressing the edges to seal.
Crimp the edges with a fork to seal the empanada.
Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.
Place the empanadas on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and brush with egg wash.
Bake in a preheated oven until golden brown, about 20 minutes.
Serve the empanadas hot with the bechamel sauce for dipping.
Cook ground beef to an internal temperature of 71°C / 160°F (no longer pink in the middle) before serving.
